claims.text: A second congressional proceeding, the House Committee on Science and Astronautics 'Symposium on Unidentified Flying Objects', was held on 29 July 1968 with witnesses including J. Allen Hynek, James E. McDonald and Carl Sagan.

claims.sourceText: US House Committee on Science and Astronautics, 'Symposium on Unidentified Flying Objects', 90th Congress, 2nd Session, 29 July 1968
claims.text: Hynek testified before the House Committee on Science and Astronautics at its UFO symposium on 29 July 1968, alongside James E. McDonald, Carl Sagan, Robert L. Hall, James A. Harder and Robert M. L. Baker Jr.

claims.sourceText: US House Committee on Science and Astronautics, 'Symposium on Unidentified Flying Objects', 90th Congress, 2nd Session, 29 July 1968
claims.text: McDonald testified before the House Committee on Science and Astronautics on 29 July 1968 as senior physicist at the University of Arizona Institute of Atmospheric Physics.

edges.label: Both testified at the 29 July 1968 congressional symposium
edges.note: The Air Force's own long-serving consultant and its most aggressive scientific critic appeared at the same hearing, both concluding the official program was inadequate.

edges.label: McDonald reviewed Blue Book files and told Congress it was not an investigation
edges.note: Testifying on 29 July 1968 he told the House Science and Astronautics Committee that 'credible observers are observing relatively incredible objects' and that the subject deserved science rather than ridicule.

b.label: University of Colorado UFO Project (Condon Committee)

edges.label: McDonald attacked the Condon Report and was professionally destroyed
edges.note: He publicly criticised the report on release, was ridiculed over his UFO work during 1971 congressional SST hearings on an unrelated technical subject, and died by suicide in June 1971.
